description.narrative: Isiolo County is one of the Counties in the Upper Eastern region of Kenya and covers an area of approximately 25,700 km2. It has an estimated population of 143, 294 .The county which is classified as arid and semi-arid (ASAL) is hot and dry in most months in the year with two rainy seasons: short rains in October and November; long rains in March and May. The rainfall is unreliable with an annual average of 580.2 mm. The County like other ASAL areas is grappling with numerous socio-economic challenges manifested in among other indicators food insecurity, low incomes, unemployment, environmental degradation and inter-community conflicts. In view of these, the key needs of the communities are: Food security: constitutes a key challenge facing the pastoral and Agro-Pastoral communities in Isiolo County. The County has a food poverty rate of 77%. Majority of the people depend primarily on relief food. Over 80% of the land in the County is non-arable (22,000 km2) and is used for grazing by the pastoralists. Only 1,497 hectares are under food crops production . Environmental management: The scarce resources in Isiolo County lead to severe environmental degradation of land and pasture that immensely contribute to the often-experienced inter-ethnic conflicts. Charcoal burning, sand harvesting, overgrazing and overstocking in most parts of the county has been rapidly depleting vegetation leaving land exposed to soil erosion. Environmental degradation has led to decreased vegetation cover; water scarcity due to destruction of water catchments, increase of environment-related diseases such as kalaazar, eyes and respiratory problems. Conflicts: Isiolo County is prone to inter and intra community conflicts triggered by among other factors competition for scarce resources such as pasture and water, cattle rustling, negative perceptions, boundary disputes and political instigations.
